Typography

A consistent type system with headings, body text, font weight utilities, alignment, truncation, lists, blockquotes, code, and display headings.

Headings

ZAKUIKit provides styled heading tags h1 through h6, plus matching .zak-h1–.zak-h6 classes that can be applied to any element.

Headings

Heading 1

Heading 2

Heading 3

Heading 4

Heading 5
Heading 6
html 
<h1>Heading 1</h1>
<h2>Heading 2</h2>
<h3>Heading 3</h3>
<h4>Heading 4</h4>
<h5>Heading 5</h5>
<h6>Heading 6</h6>

<!-- Classes can be applied to any element -->
<span class="zak-h3">Faux heading</span>

Body Text

Standard paragraphs, lead text, small text, and inline text elements.

Body text

This is lead text. It draws attention to the opening line or summary of a section.

This is standard body text. It is used for most content across the interface and uses the default font size, line-height, and color.

This is small text, and this is bold text, italic text, and highlighted text.

Inline code: npm install, keyboard input: Ctrl+C, and a link.

html 
<p class="zak-lead">Lead text</p>
<p>Body text</p>
<p><small>Small text</small> <strong>Bold</strong> <em>Italic</em> <code>code</code> <kbd>kbd</kbd></p>

<!-- Font size utilities -->
.zak-fs-xs .zak-fs-sm .zak-fs-base .zak-fs-lg
.zak-fs-xl .zak-fs-2xl .zak-fs-3xl .zak-fs-4xl .zak-fs-5xl

Font Weights

Control font weight with utility classes from lightweight to extra bold.

Weights
Light (300) Normal (400) Medium (500) Semibold (600) Bold (700)
css 
/* Utility classes */
.zak-fw-light     { font-weight: 300; }
.zak-fw-normal    { font-weight: 400; }
.zak-fw-medium    { font-weight: 500; }
.zak-fw-semibold  { font-weight: 600; }
.zak-fw-bold      { font-weight: 700; }

/* Font family */
.zak-font-sans  .zak-font-serif  .zak-font-mono

/* Line heights */
.zak-lh-none .zak-lh-tight .zak-lh-snug .zak-lh-normal
.zak-lh-relaxed .zak-lh-loose

/* Letter spacing */
.zak-tracking-tight .zak-tracking-wide .zak-tracking-wider .zak-tracking-widest

Text Alignment

Align text with left, center, right, and justify utilities.

Alignment

Left-aligned text (zak-text-start).

Center-aligned text (zak-text-center).

Right-aligned text (zak-text-end).

Justified text (zak-text-justify). Justified text stretches to fill both the left and right margins, which can improve readability in narrow columns but may create uneven spacing between words.

html 
<p class="zak-text-start">Left</p>
<p class="zak-text-center">Center</p>
<p class="zak-text-end">Right</p>
<p class="zak-text-justify">Justify</p>

Text Transformation

Change text case with transform utilities.

Transformation
Uppercase text LOWERCASE TEXT capitalize each word
html 
<span class="zak-uppercase">UPPERCASE</span>
<span class="zak-lowercase">lowercase</span>
<span class="zak-capitalize">Capitalize</span>

<!-- Also available -->
.zak-text-decoration-none .zak-text-underline .zak-text-line-through

Text Truncation

Truncate single-line text with zak-text-truncate, or control wrapping with zak-text-break and zak-text-nowrap.

Truncation

This is a very long line of text that will be truncated to a single line with an ellipsis at the end.

ThisIsAVeryLongUnbrokenStringWithoutSpacesThatWillBeBrokenToPreventOverflowingItsContainingBox

html 
<!-- Single-line truncation -->
<p class="zak-text-truncate">Long text that gets clipped...</p>

<!-- Multi-line / wrapping -->
<p class="zak-text-wrap">Normal wrapping</p>
<p class="zak-text-nowrap">No wrapping</p>
<p class="zak-text-break">Breaks long words</p>

Styled blockquotes for citations and featured quotes.

Blockquote
"Design is not just what it looks like and feels like. Design is how it works."
— Steve Jobs

</blockquote>

Code

Inline code and pre-formatted code blocks.

Code

Use inline code for short snippets, and <pre> blocks for multi-line examples.

<div class="zak-container">
  <h1>Hello, ZAKUIKit!</h1>
</div>
html 
<p>Inline <code>code</code> snippet</p>

<pre><code><div class="zak-container">...</div></code></pre>

Accessibility

  • Always use the correct semantic heading level (h1–h6) to reflect the document structure; zak-h* classes are for visual matching only.
  • Maintain a minimum text contrast of 4.5:1 against the background.
  • When truncating text, consider providing a title attribute or the full text for screen readers.
  • Do not use bold or italic formatting (b, strong, em) purely for visual style — reserve them for their semantic meaning.
  • Line height should be at least 1.5 for body text to improve readability.
